invariants: Every new or changed English string gets a Welsh draft beside it in the same change, as the service's other copy does.

Every changed page works fully without JavaScript: every state change is a form post, every search and filter a form with a button that submits it, and JavaScript only enhances a page that already works (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 6; conflicts:c-006).

A behaviour is built with GOV.UK Frontend first, then another tested government library (Ministry of Justice, HMRC, Scottish Government); no custom JavaScript is written to copy the prototype, pop-ups are not built and confirmations stay pages (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 5, 7 and 19).
Pages are built from GOV.UK Frontend components and govuk-* classes; the prototype's custom app-dr2-* blocks are not copied.

A search box is the real frontend's accessible autocomplete over a native select and behaves as the real frontend configures it; its entries are what MDM serves through reference-data, and only how the list reads follows the prototype (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 1 to 4).

Where a row changes a page or behaviour the high-risk plants frontend also has, the same increment changes plants too: plants mirrors the structure, wording patterns, components and behaviour, and keeps its own questions, data and step order (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 43 and 44).
Shared wording in a frontend's shared copy is never reworded in place; a set-specific string goes in the feature's own copy (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 41).

Notification statuses are only ever added, never renamed or removed, and each new status is mapped in every frontend that reads it before the animals backend first sends it (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 42).
A page in its error state keeps the 'Error: ' prefix on its browser title (conflicts:c-006).

Every save control a page offers makes exactly the same checks on that page's answers, with no page an exception: a missing or invalid answer keeps the trader on the page with an error for each one and what they entered still shown, and the controls differ only in where they go once every answer passes (ruling:sam-2026-10-26).
Notifications, templates and address book entries stay scoped to the signed-in user's organisation (or user, for templates); nothing lists another organisation's records.
Each increment updates the tests repo's specs, page objects and journey helpers its change breaks, in the same change.

increments.title: Live animals browser tests prove how pages look by screenshot, accessible name and GOV.UK values read at run time
increments.detail: Many live animals browser tests still prove looks by class list, fixed alignment, line height or a hard-coded colour, and find buttons and boxes by class. That breaks the programme rule that a browser test never writes a fixed style and compares only with GOV.UK values read at run time or a screenshot. The tests move to accessible names and roles, the looks they stop asserting move to the screenshot suite, the type-aheads gain accented searches, and shared test steps keep only what more than one spec uses.
acceptanceCriteria: Every live animals browser test that checks how a page looks proves it by a screenshot, by position or size against another element, or by a value read from GOV.UK at run time. None writes a fixed colour, pixel size, line height, text alignment or class list. (loop:design-snagging-followups inc-225 followUps[8]; inc-226 followUps[0]-[5], [13]; inc-228 followUps[1])

The live animals browser tests find the arrival details labels, the Upload documents actions, the transporter tags and legends and the type-ahead buttons by role, accessible name or heading, not by class. (loop:design-snagging-followups inc-226 followUps[2], [4], [13]; ruling:sam-2026-11-10b)

The screenshot suite shows the looks those tests stop asserting: the arrival details medium labels and the Upload documents actions column right-aligned. (loop:design-snagging-followups inc-226 followUps[1], [3]; ruling:sam-2026-11-10b)

Each live animals type-ahead is proven in the browser to offer a matching name when the trader's search and the name differ only by accents, with the matching letters in bold. (loop:design-snagging-followups inc-228 followUps[4])

A browser-test step, reader or selector used by one spec lives in that spec, and one used by several has a single owner. The live animals testing guide lists as shared only the steps more than one spec uses. (loop:design-snagging-followups inc-225 followUps[8]; inc-226 followUps[10], [11])
Every live animals browser test and the animals screenshot suite pass, on both screenshot baselines. (loop:design-snagging-followups inc-226)

openQuestions: The two new tests-repo screenshot specs (tests/animals/e2e/visual/arrival-details.visual.spec.ts and upload-documents.visual.spec.ts) have no chromium-linux or chromium-darwin baseline PNGs, so toHaveScreenshot fails on first run and criteria 3 and 6 are unmet. Making them needs the workspace stack, which this build run does not hold: take the linux images from the tests repo PR CI artefact once a person has looked at them, make the darwin ones with test:visual:update:macos on a stack-held run, and commit both into the -snapshots directories before the row lands. Until then nothing proves the arrival details medium labels or the Upload documents actions column right-aligned. (Review findings: missing visual baselines for arrival-details and upload-documents.)

For a person: the live animals type-ahead paints its focused input inset shadow in currentColor, which resolves to rgb(0, 0, 0), while GOV.UK paints the focused input shadow in --govuk-input-border-colour, rgb(11, 12, 12) (govuk-frontend.min.css .govuk-input:focus; accessible-autocomplete.min.css). Should the type-ahead stylesheet paint the focus shadow in GOV.UK input-border colour (a production change on signed-off pages), or keep the current colour? Until ruled, the focus test in type-ahead.fit.spec.js pins the shadow to the input text colour and GOV.UK shadow geometry as read. (Review finding: type-ahead focus test strips the shadow colour.)
